answer: Copper-Weighted Correlation Pricing. Each new identity must anchor its first action to an existing identity's activity record, and every action is charged a price proportional to the correlation between its claimed independent behavior and its anchor's observed pattern. Clones inherit their anchor's pricing tier, so a whisper of identical timing or shared counterparties sharply raises fees. Enforcement: when correlation exceeds threshold, all linked identities pay the escalated rate, making each clone cost strictly more than the marginal revenue it can capture.
